    depot = instance["depot_index"]

    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]
    vehicle_hint = instance.get("vehicle_count_hint", 0) or 0

    def route_load(route):
        s = 0
        for node in route:
            s += demands[node]
        return s

        if not route:

        c = matrix[depot][route[0]] + matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        for a, b in zip(route, route[1:]):
            c += matrix[a][b]
        return c

    def total_cost(routes):
        return sum(route_cost(r) for r in routes)

    # Start with single-customer routes
    customers = sorted(customers_set)
    routes = []

    savings_list = []
    for a_i, i in enumerate(customers):
        di = matrix[depot][i]

            sij = di + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
            sji = di = None  # dummy to keep structure small
            # We'll use both directions as separate merge candidates (endpoint orientation matters)
            savings_list.append((sij, i, j))
            sij2 = matrix[depot][j] + matrix[depot][i] - matrix[j][i]
            savings_list.append((sij2, j, i))
    savings_list.sort(key=lambda t: (-t[0], t[1], t[2]))

    max_merges = len(customers) - desired_routes if vehicle_hint > 0 else len(customers)
    merges_done = 0

    def is_route_end(route_idx, node):
        r = routes[route_idx]
        return r and (r[0] == node or r[-1] == node)

    def is_left_end(route_idx, node):
        return routes[route_idx] and routes[route_idx][0] == node

    def is_right_end(route_idx, node):
        return routes[route_idx] and routes[route_idx][-1] == node
